entities.name: PMID:27498017
observations: Nationwide cross-sectional retrospective medical-record audit in 2009–2010 involving 1,168 patients with spondyloarthritis across 45 centres.
Adjusted multilevel analyses found centre characteristics contributed to variation in rheumatology ambulatory care and referrals to other specialties.

entities.name: Spondyloarthritis
observations: Study population was predominantly ankylosing spondylitis and psoriatic arthritis patients receiving rheumatology care.

entities.name: Centre-care variation
observations: Adjusted between-centre variability was 15.7% for rheumatology-clinic attendance and 12.3% for referrals to other specialties.
Referral probability differed by up to 25% according to treating centre.
Faculty and trainee numbers partly explained rheumatology attendance variation; urban setting, number of procedures, and dedicated spondyloarthritis clinics were associated with referral variation.
